title: Dilworth's theorem, hard direction: min chain cover = max antichain, via the down-set/up-set decomposition

problemStatement.formal: For a finite poset on ground Finset s, if every antichain A ⊆ s has A.card ≤ w, then s admits a chain cover by ≤ w chains. With w = max antichain width and the easy direction (antichain_card_le_of_chainCover), this gives min chain cover = max antichain.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the hard (attainment) direction of Dilworth's theorem via the Galvin/Perles down-set/up-set decomposition. Mathlib has neither Dilworth nor the centralizer-style machinery; only the easy direction and the dual (Mirsky) hard direction exist in the gallery.
whyMatters: Dilworth's theorem is a cornerstone of order theory and combinatorics, absent from Mathlib.
Completes the chain/antichain duality whose easy direction and Mirsky dual are already in the gallery.

currentState.focus: Galvin/Perles induction: down-set/up-set decomposition of a maximum antichain, then glue inductive sub-covers.
blockers: Degenerate case downSet A s = A (A = set of minimal elements) makes upSet A s = s, so the up-set recursion does not strictly shrink; needs the dual argument or a thin-poset base case.
Bookkeeping that each size-w sub-cover meets the maximum antichain in exactly one element per chain (bijection A ↔ sub-cover).

insights: Mathlib has neither Dilworth's theorem nor König's theorem (max matching = min vertex cover); it does have Hall's marriage theorem (SimpleGraph/Hall) and SimpleGraph matching API, so a Hall/König route is possible but the matching↔chain-cover bridge is itself substantial.

The gallery already has the easy direction (DilworthTheoremOQ01.antichain_card_le_of_chainCover) and the HARD direction of the DUAL (Mirsky) via height/level decomposition (DilworthMirskyHardOQ01); Mirsky's clean height trick does NOT transfer to Dilworth.
Strong form (antichain bound w ⟹ chain cover ≤ w) is the right statement for induction: removing elements only shrinks antichains, so the hypothesis is inherited by sub-posets.
Down-set/up-set of a MAXIMUM antichain A satisfy downSet ∩ upSet = A and downSet ∪ upSet = s (the union needs maximality: a missed element would enlarge A). These are proved unconditionally.

A chain inside downSet through a' ∈ A lies entirely ≤ a' (antichain forces the witness to be a'); dually for upSet. Hence a down-set chain and an up-set chain through the same a' glue into one chain — the inductive assembly step.

The genuine difficulty (why Dilworth is absent from Mathlib and was a Coq-paper result, Singh–Natarajan arXiv:1703.06133) is the degenerate case downSet A s = A: then upSet = s and the recursion stalls; A is exactly the set of minimal elements. Dual degeneracy (A = maximal elements) is the mirror. Resolving both requires a symmetric/dual argument plus a thin-poset base case (s an antichain ⟹ singleton cover).
